heading: Tell Tachyon who is signed in
body: A project with `SignedIn` or `Allow` routes has exactly one class marked `IdentityProvider`, in `server/controllers/<Name>IdentityProvider.<ext>`. It is like a Spring `AuthenticationProvider`. Its one method, `identify` (`Identify` in C# and Go), takes the request in the language's own type and returns the signed-in user with the names of their roles, such as `{ "user": "ada", "roles": ["Admin"] }`, or no value when nobody is signed in. It may also read one header or cookie with `FromHeader` or `FromCookie`. Tachyon calls it before every `SignedIn` or `Allow` route, in any Yon language. When `identify` returns no value, Tachyon answers 401. When the user has none of the roles, Tachyon answers 403. In both cases the route method never runs. When `identify` fails, Tachyon answers 500 and the route method does not run either. A `SignedIn` or `Allow` route without an identity provider, a second identity provider, or an `Allow` role with no type in `server/roles/` stops the build with `TY1322` or `TY1323`. A test unit calls a controller method directly, so no identity is needed there. To test the identity provider itself, a test unit builds it and fakes its collaborators with `@Fake`.
